title: Louisiana Lost Land the Size of Rhode Island. One Corner Is Growing.
description:
Louisiana land loss is one of the fastest coastal changes in the United States: since the 1950s the state has lost wetlands the size of Rhode Island. Yet in one corner of the coast, the Atchafalaya Basin, the land is growing. Here is what 36 years of Landsat data show, and how NASA's Delta-X mission, with boats, waders and three planes, is working out why.

In this episode:
0:00 Louisiana is losing land
0:18 What Landsat measured
0:35 Why the marsh drowned
0:55 The corner that grows
1:07 Delta-X goes in by boat
1:25 Three planes overhead
1:46 Can the wetlands recover?
1:56 Why deltas matter worldwide
